My professor was impressed with it, especially the art, animations, and characters, which I all created myself using the app ibisPaint. My family was also impressed as well. It's the first game I've ever created from scratch.

Charcoal still life drawing that I made for a college art course assignment. I would say it's the closest I've ever gotten to hitting photorealism with traditional art. It was praised by my teacher and classmates which I of course felt achievement because of.

I had a short story about the migration of monarch butterflies with accompanying drawings printed out and displayed when I was in 2nd grade. My teacher gushed to my parents about how well I did and how smart I was for my age. I know this sounds dumb but I put a lot of effort into it, and it was the first time anyone had ever said I did a good job on anything I think, so it meant a lot to me.

I wrote several Tumblr stories about my own life, and then replaced myself and the people involved with various characters and was able to make quite a bit of money off the audience. I think I built a really large following and a lot of people paid me to write different short stories with their favorite characters in them. It was nice to see that people liked the things I wrote.

I made an anniversary magazine for my significant other using Canva, and sort of did different layouts/spreads for different aspects of our relationship. I'm super into asking hypothetical questions, so I had him ask me some and I did a Q&A style layout. I also did one of trips I wanted to take with him and cut out little clay dolls and made it look like they were traveling. I spent a lot of time and effort on it and I guess I didn't get as much of a reaction as I wanted but I was happy to look at it all and it made me feel good about myself to express love and care for someone through art.

I created a browser extension for baseball fans. It allowed you to see a baseball player's advanced stats easily without having to go to another tab. It has one 5 star review on Mozilla so far. My Discord mates praised me for it.

I created a puzzle for a Twitch streamer. I used a picture of their cats they had taken earlier in the year. I edited the picture to remove the distractions. She was shocked once she had opened it. Everyone in her chat was hyped once she had opened it.
A musician was making a music video in Blender. I suggested 2 videos to put in the music video. They used both. They both made it to the final cut. The video has had thousands of views.

In my case, I wanted to learn how to make my own creative designs for rugs and stuck with it for two years. One of the designs I did was some Arabic lettering that I liked, both for its aesthetic appeal and for the meaning of the phrase itself. A friend of mine, who is Muslim, owns several boutique shops throughout North America for his clothing brand that is centered around Egyptian cotton from the Nile Delta. His culture and homeland is central to the brand's identity, and he ended up asking if I could make something similar for him (something in Arabic).
